why: The feature-length-episode rule (compare-spec 2.19.0; operator, 2026-10-03) makes an Episode over an hour a candidate for a Basic TV movie ONLY when the episode carries a USER-SUPPLIED title. A system-generated title (built by the registry from the parent's title and the episode's number) says nothing a TV movie's title can be matched against, so a long episode that has only one is not a candidate, however its text reads. Asked for by De-Dupe UI's mutation test of 2.19.0 (relayed by eidr-core, 2026-10-08): moving the length test outside the user-title requirement survived all 40 fixtures, because the only fixture for the rule has a user title. Here the episode runs 95 minutes and its only title is system-generated, with the SAME text as the Basic's title so that a title-blind implementation scores the pair as a strong candidate. Expected: not a candidate (Reject). Pair with crosstype-feature-length-episode-meets-tv-movie-at-review, the same shape with a user title, which must reach Review; an implementation that drops the user-title requirement passes that one and fails this one.
